This application coming on for admission this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER

This is the first bail application filed on behalf of the applicant/accused under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail, as he is under apprehension of his arrest, in connection with Crime No.643/2023, registered at Police Station Shahjehanabad, District Bhopal (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467 and 468 of Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2. As per prosecution story, applicant's son Karan Grover was married to one Gauri daughter of Raman Govardhan Arora.
Raman Govardhan Arora is owner of company namely Search Smart Logistics Private Limited along with his wife Sangeeta Arora.
Said company was acquired by complainant.

After marriage of complainant's daughter with applicant's son, applicant Ved Prakash Grover was appointed as honorary Director of company without there being any consideration paid Ved Prakash Grover vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72960249/

sentences.text: His residential address was recorded with Registrar of companies.
Thereafter, dishonesty crept in the minds of applicant.
Applicant along with one Aagam Jain called meeting of Board of Directors on 11.03.2020 and forged a resolution.
Signature of complainant and his wife was forged for getting wrongful gains.
As per said resolution, applicant is to be paid salary of Rs.1,50,000/- per month.
Sangeeta Arora was made Director of the company on 15.06.2020.
She was not Director of the company on 11.03.2020 which also points that resolution was forged.

Aagam Jain has given an affidavit that Board meeting was called on insistence of applicant Ved Prakash Grover and signature of complainant and his wife was pasted on board resolution by using computer tools of cut, copy and paste.
Prosecution also alleged that applicant is trying to extort salary of 27 months i.e. Rs.40 lacs from company and complainant and has also filed an application to D.C.P. Zone-3 on 11.08.2023.
3. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for applicant submitted that there is matrimonial dispute between son of applicant Karan and daughter of complainant namely Gauri.
Wife lodged an FIR under Section 498-A of Indian Penal Code against the applicant and her husband.
Applicant's son has filed a petition for divorce.
Applicant has invested a huge sum of money in the company and applicant had Rs.9,48,000/- shares in company.
Complainant Raman Govardhan Arora and his wife played fraud with applicant.

They forged share transfer form to cheat the applicant and shares belonging to applicant were transferred in favour of Shri Raman Govardhan Arora and Sangeeta Raman Arora without his consent and without paying any consideration with intent to get undue monetary gains by illegal means.

Applicant filed a complaint at Police Station Shahjehanabad,
Bhopal on 15.05.2023 disclosing all material facts and providing all documentary proof to police.
Complaint was also made to Registrar of company.
Board resolution dated 11.03.2020 was never forged and fabricated by applicant.
Complainant himself supplied the Board resolution on 11.03.2020 to applicant and later on, same was termed to be forged.
It is submitted that applicant had filed a different board resolution in bail application which does not have signature of the applicant.

However, in forged board resolution there was signature of applicant which shows that document was forged by complainant acting hand in glove with Aagam Jain to falsely implicate the applicant in the case.
Applicant did not get any financial benefit from Board resolution dated 11.03.2020.
Applicant is a reputed person and a senior citizen.
He will cooperate in investigation of the case.
In these circumstances, he may be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
4. Government Advocate appearing for State opposed the application for grant of anticipatory bail and submitted that applicant had forged the board resolution dated 11.03.2020.
Offence under section 467, 468, 471 and 420 of IPC is made out against the applicant and offences are serious in nature and punishable up to life imprisonment.
Applicant was declared as proclaimed offender by police and prize money is also offered on his arrest.
Reliance was also placed on proclamation dated 11.01.2024 by which prize money of Rs.3000/- was declared for arrest of applicant.
In these circumstances, prayer is made for dismissal of application of anticipatory bail.
5. Counsel appearing for objector opposed the application for grant of anticipatory bail.
It is submitted by the counsel for the objector that S.S.L. Company was acquired by complainant/objector from erstwhile Director one Smt. Pinki Jain and Shri Siddharth Saxena.
Applicant was only honorary director of the company without there being any investment by him.

Applicant had misused the forged document.
Employee of company Aagam Jain has also given an affidavit that applicant had forged the document.
He has also submitted a letter of apology.
Sangeeta Arora was inducted as Director on 15.06.2020 and as she was not Director, therefore, she could not have signed Board of resolution dated 11.03.2020.
6. Counsel appearing for respondents also placed reliance on additional document filed by him and on basis of said document submitted that number of capital of the Company were 10000 shares.

Pinky Jain owned 9900 shares of Rs.10/- each and Shdidharth Saxena had 100 shares of Rs.10/-
each, total 10000/-.
Later said Company was taken over by complainant.
As on 31.12.2022, there were three directors namely Ved Prakash Grover, Raman Arora & Sangita Arora.
Applicant-Ved Prakash Grover was only honorary Directer only for purpose of convenience and no share was assigned to him.
Marksmen Automobile Private Limited had given unsecured loan to the Company of Rs.90 Lacs.
Said facts discernible from report of Board of Directors dated 31.03.2020 presented in AGM.

Applicant himself has furnished form 16-A and certificate under Section 203 of Income Tax Act for S.S.L. Company and tax of Rs.1,03,940/- was deposited by Marksmen Automobile Private Limited through applicant.
Annual return of S.S.L. Company was also submitted before Registrar of Companies by applicant on 30.11.2021.

In said annual return (Form No.MGT-7), statement of capital was given, in which, it has been stated that there are 10000 shares in total in the beginning of the year and said shares have increased to 4,74,000 and Ved Prakash Grover was shown to be holding 0 equity shares and Raman Govardhan was holding 28,54,000 shares and Sangita Raman was holding 18,19,000/- as on 30.11.2021, therefore, no share was transferred illegally from Company in name of complainant and applicant was also aware of said fact.
Applicant had forged the Board Resolution to gain wrongfully.
In these circumstances, applicant may not be granted anticipatory bail.

7. Heard learned counsel for parties.
8.
On going through the factual matrix of case, it is clear that Company was acquired by Raman Govardhan Arora and shares were held by Sangita Raman Arora and Raman Govardhan Arora.
Sangita Raman Arora was not Member of Board of Directors, when board resolution was passed on 11.03.2020.
One Angam Jain has given an affidavit that forgery was done at the instance of applicant.

Applicant is said to have signed on the document knowing the document to be forged,
therefore, it cannot be said that applicant is not maker of document in question.
Learned Sr.

Counsel appearing for applicant submitted that he had filed a complaint before Registrar of Companies regarding transfer of shares, therefore, he has been implicated but annual return statement which was filed in the year 2021 shows that applicant was not holding any share in the Company.
The amount which has been transferred by applicant to SSL Company was shown to be loan amount and no shares have been allotted to him.
Applicant failed to file any document to show that he hold shares in company which has been transferred to complainant.
Applicant will be required for investigation of the case.
Offence said to have been committed by applicant is serious in nature and requires investigation.
Learned Sr. counsel appearing for applicant further argued that there was no monitory gains to the applicant as no money has been received by him.

By resolution of Company, applicant was to be given salary of Rs.1.50 as Director and, therefore, said document is a Ved Prakash Grover vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72960249/

Whether,
applicant has gained out of it or not is not a question at present and further investigation will reveal that what were the wrongful gains of the applicant.

Since applicant has signed the document, which as per allegations, he knows to be false, therefore, by signing the document, applicant has also become a party to making of a document, therefore, it cannot be said that offence under Section 467 of IPC is not made out against applicant.
9. In view of above discussion, applicant for grant of anticipatory bail is dismissed.
